issues.claim: The server then sends its certificate and signs the handshake
issues.problem: CertificateVerify signs a hash of the handshake messages so far (ClientHello through Certificate), not the whole handshake. Verified at tls13.xargs.org and RFC 8446; the simplification does not mislead.
issues.fix: The server then sends its certificate and signs the handshake so far, proving it holds the private key.

issues.claim: After that, everything is encrypted, so only the endpoints can read it.
issues.problem: The RFC says the data sent over the channel is visible only to the endpoints. The hello messages are plaintext, and metadata such as IP addresses and message sizes stays visible. 'Everything' is loose. Handshake encryption after ServerHello is confirmed by Wikipedia and tls13.xargs.org.
issues.fix: After that, your data is encrypted, so only the two endpoints can read it.

issues.problem: TLS 1.3 derives several keys from one shared secret, and the 'anyone watches' framing assumes a passive observer. Rhetorical simplification only.
issues.fix: Your browser and a server agree on secret keys while anyone can watch the traffic.
